To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the renormalization group (RG) invariance of the chiral nuclear force is a powerful constraint that allows us to determine the power counting of the counterterms; (2) the power counting of counterterms in the triplet channels of the chiral nucleon-nucleus potential is different from that in the singlet channel, and is enhanced as much as that of the leading one-pion exchange potential.
the power counting for the subleading contact terms in the triplet channels is different from Weinberg’s original scheme.
the power counting of the chiral effective field theories of nuclear forces is renormalization-group invariant.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the renormalization of the chiral nuclear force, with the focus on the subleading counterterm of the triplet channels.
the subleading contact terms of the triplet channels in chiral effective field theories.
the renormalization of the chiral effective field theories of nucleon-nuclear interactions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

WPC is a consistent power counting for the nucleon-nucleus scattering problem in the framework of effective field theory, provided that the subleading counterterm Lagrangian is modified to include the leading-order counterterms of the triplet channels.

, with renormalization group (RG) as the constraint, the power counting of Weinberg’s original counting scheme (WPC) is valid only in the 3 S1 and 3 D1 channels, and in the 3 P1 channel, WPC is modified in such a way that the subleading counterterm is enhanced by a factor of 1 / m π.

WPC is the most natural and convenient choice of the power counting scheme in the triplet channels, and the renormalization group invariant (RGI) power counting is a natural and convenient choice in the singlet channels.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that the renormalized nuclear force is not unique, and that the renormalization procedure can be used to modify the original chiral power counting scheme.

, in chiral nuclear forces, the power counting of the leading order (LO) and next-to-leading order (NLO) counterterms are fixed by renormalization group (RG) invariance and the power counting for the subleading counterterm is fixed by the modified version of the naive dimensional analysis.
the renormalization group provides a natural framework for the power counting of chiral nuclear forces.
The main takeaway from our work is that
renormalization group arguments are crucial to understanding the renormalization of nuclear forces.
the subleading order counterterms are not negligible in the triplet channels and should be included in the analysis.
, when compared to the WPC, the power counting in the triplet channels is modified by the singular attraction of the one-pion exchange.
